title: 5 Signs Your AC Needs Servicing in {{CITY_NAME}}
metaDescription: Not cooling, water leakage, bad odour or high electricity bills? Here are 5 clear signs your AC needs professional servicing in {{CITY_NAME}}.
excerpt: From weak cooling to rising electricity bills — here's how to tell your AC is overdue for a service, and what a technician actually checks in {{CITY_NAME}}.
bodyHtml:
Air conditioners rarely stop working all at once — they usually give warning signs for weeks before a full breakdown. Catching these early in {{CITY_NAME}}'s weather can save you an emergency repair bill later.

1. Weak or warm airflow

If your AC is running but the room isn't cooling like it used to, the most common cause is low refrigerant gas or a dirty filter restricting airflow. Both are quick fixes during a routine service.

2. Water leaking from the indoor unit

A blocked drain pipe is the usual culprit. Left unattended, this can damage your wall or ceiling — it's one of the most common service calls we get in {{CITY_NAME}}.

3. Unusual noise or smell

Rattling, buzzing, or a musty smell when you switch it on usually points to a loose part or mould buildup inside the unit — both are addressed during a standard service visit.

4. Rising electricity bills

A poorly maintained AC has to work harder to cool the same space, which shows up directly on your electricity bill. Regular servicing keeps it running efficiently.

5. It's been more than 4-6 months

Even if nothing seems wrong, dust and grime build up inside every AC over time — especially in {{CITY_NAME}}'s dustier months. A service every 4-6 months keeps it running at peak efficiency and extends its life.

If any of these sound familiar, a verified Seerua technician can inspect and service your AC in {{CITY_NAME}} with transparent, upfront pricing — no hidden charges.

title: How Often Should You Service Your RO Water Purifier in {{CITY_NAME}}?
metaDescription: Wondering how often to service your RO purifier in {{CITY_NAME}}? Here's the honest answer based on filter life, water quality, and usage.
excerpt: RO filters don't last forever, and water quality in {{CITY_NAME}} plays a bigger role than you'd think. Here's a simple, honest servicing schedule.
bodyHtml:
Unlike an AC or washing machine, an RO purifier's parts wear out on a fairly predictable schedule — mainly because they're constantly filtering incoming water quality, which varies a lot depending on your source and area in {{CITY_NAME}}.

Sediment & pre-filters: every 3-4 months

These catch the first, heaviest layer of dirt and rust from the water supply. In areas of {{CITY_NAME}} with harder or more turbid water, this can need attention even sooner.

RO membrane: every 12-18 months

This is the core filtering component. A worn-out membrane doesn't just reduce output — it can let more dissolved impurities through without you noticing, since the water still looks and tastes normal.

UV lamp: every 12 months

If your purifier has UV disinfection, the lamp's germicidal effectiveness drops over time even if it still lights up. It needs yearly replacement regardless of how much water has passed through.

Signs you shouldn't ignore

Slow water flow, a change in taste, or the purifier running much longer than usual to fill a glass are all signs it's overdue for a service — don't wait for a full breakdown.

A Seerua technician in {{CITY_NAME}} can check all of this in a single visit and only replace what's actually needed — transparent pricing, no unnecessary upsells.

title: Washing Machine Not Draining? Common Causes & Fixes in {{CITY_NAME}}
metaDescription: Washing machine stuck with water inside after a wash cycle? Here are the most common causes in {{CITY_NAME}} homes and when to call a technician.
excerpt: Water stuck inside the drum after a cycle usually comes down to one of four things. Here's how to figure out which one before you call for repair.
bodyHtml:
A washing machine that won't drain is one of the most common repair calls we get across {{CITY_NAME}} — and thankfully, it's also one of the most fixable, once you know where to look.

1. Blocked drain filter

Almost every front-load machine has a small filter at the bottom front panel that traps coins, hair, and lint. A blocked filter is the single most common cause of drainage issues — and the easiest to fix.

2. Kinked or blocked drain hose

If the hose behind the machine is bent, pinched, or has something stuck inside it, water has nowhere to go. Worth checking before assuming it's a bigger fault.

3. Faulty drain pump

If you hear a humming sound but no water is being pushed out, the drain pump motor itself may have failed. This needs a technician visit to diagnose and replace safely.

4. Overloading the machine

Cramming in too many clothes can prevent the drum from spinning properly, which in turn affects draining. Try a smaller, lighter load and see if the issue persists.

If checking the filter and hose doesn't solve it, it's best to get a professional to look at the pump and internal wiring — a Seerua technician in {{CITY_NAME}} can usually diagnose this within the same visit.

title: Fridge Not Cooling? Quick Troubleshooting Guide for {{CITY_NAME}} Homes
metaDescription: Fridge running but not cooling properly? Try these quick checks before booking a repair in {{CITY_NAME}} — plus signs it needs a technician.
excerpt: Before you assume the worst, a few quick checks can tell you whether it's a simple fix or something that needs a technician's attention.
bodyHtml:
A fridge that's running (you can hear the compressor) but not actually cooling is confusing — and the cause can range from a two-minute fix to something that needs a technician. Here's how to narrow it down.

Check the thermostat setting first

It sounds obvious, but the thermostat dial can get accidentally bumped, especially in busy kitchens. Make sure it's set to a mid-range cooling level and give it a few hours to stabilise.

Look at the door seal

A worn or loose door gasket lets cold air escape continuously, forcing the compressor to run constantly without ever reaching the set temperature. Run a piece of paper along the seal — if it slides out easily, the seal needs replacing.

Clean the condenser coils

Dust buildup on the coils at the back or bottom of the fridge is extremely common, especially in {{CITY_NAME}}'s dustier seasons, and it directly reduces cooling efficiency.

When it needs a technician

If the compressor isn't running at all, you hear clicking sounds, or cooling doesn't improve after the checks above, the issue is likely with the compressor, gas charge, or wiring — this needs a professional diagnosis rather than a DIY fix.

A Seerua technician in {{CITY_NAME}} can inspect the gas pressure, compressor, and wiring in one visit, with the exact repair cost shared before any work begins.

title: AMC vs One-Time Repair: What's Better for {{CITY_NAME}} Homes?
metaDescription: Should you get an Annual Maintenance Contract or pay per repair? Here's a simple breakdown to help {{CITY_NAME}} homeowners decide.
excerpt: Neither option is universally 'better' — it depends on the appliance's age and how many appliances you're maintaining. Here's how to decide.
bodyHtml:
This is one of the most common questions we get from customers in {{CITY_NAME}}, and the honest answer is: it depends on two things — the appliance's age, and how many appliances you're maintaining at once.

When an AMC (Service / AMC plan) makes sense

If your appliance is under 5 years old and generally reliable, an AMC covers routine servicing (cleaning, gas top-up checks, filter changes) at a predictable cost, and often catches small issues before they become expensive repairs.

When one-time repair makes more sense

For an older appliance, or if something breaks unexpectedly and you just need it fixed once, a one-time repair is usually the more cost-effective route — you pay only for the specific issue, with no ongoing commitment.

A simple rule of thumb

If you're booking a service call more than once a year for the same appliance, an AMC will likely save you money over time. If it's a rare, one-off issue, a single repair visit is the simpler choice.

Either way, Seerua's pricing in {{CITY_NAME}} is transparent upfront — so you can compare the AMC cost against a one-time repair before deciding, with no pressure either way.
